Entries.Text: What the selected battle goal does. Set the situation, see each act's chance of being picked, and click an act to watch its animations on the character.
The script has a syntax error. Fix it to see its battle goal.
Not a battle goal: the script has no Goal.Activate.
Not a battle goal: no Goal.Activate in the script calls Common_Battle_Activate(ai, goal, weights, funcs, after[, params]).
Not a battle goal: no act is registered with REGIST_FUNC.
This battle goal has no such act table.

Activate picks the act itself: it stores each act's odds in a local, rolls, then runs the first branch of 'if roll <= w1 ... elseif roll <= w1 + w2 ...' that the roll falls in. Each branch is shown as an act, with its odds out of the total as its chance.

Activate adds its sub-goals itself, based on its own conditions and rolls, instead of picking from an act table. It is shown as one act, Activate, whose steps are what it does in the situation set. Set its rolls there to try its other branches.
The acts {0} picks from (Common_Battle_Activate). Activate calls it on some branches and plays its own sub-goals on the others.

The deflect-exchange acts that Goal.Kengeki_Activate picks from (Common_Kengeki_Activate). Activate runs it first: while the character has a Kengeki SpEffect (from ReturnKengekiSpecialEffect), it picks one of these acts and skips the normal ones. Set that SpEffect in the situation to see the weights.
The character the battle goal runs on and the target it fights, shown in the Viewport window. Remembered per binder for this session.
The character the AI fights (TARGET_ENE_0). Acts walk or run to it, turn to face it and attack it. Without one, an unseen target stands at the distance and bearing below.
The target's position in degrees from the character's front (positive to its left), measured from the character's start position.
Return the character to its start position, and the target to the set distance and bearing.
Move the target with the viewport's translate gizmo.

Play: run the goal as the game does. Goal.Activate picks an act at random by weight, the act plays (its sub-goals, then the after function's), and when it ends the goal restarts with the current situation. The distance to the target and the cooldowns come from the scene, so you can move the target with the gizmo while it runs. Stop: return to idle.
No act has any weight in this situation. Waiting, then trying again.
While the simulation runs, this comes from the scene: the distance to the target, or whether the animation played within its cooldown.

What Goal.Activate's conditions read from the game, each as its own input: numbers (distance, HP rate, random rolls), checkboxes (in front of the target, has a special effect, an animation still on cooldown) and choices (team role). Change them to see which acts the AI would pick. Click a name to show where the script reads it.
Reset every input to its starting value.
Goal.Activate's conditions read nothing from the game, so the weights never change.

Each act's chance of being picked in this situation (its share of the total weight), and what it does at the current distance to the target. Click an act to play it on the character: its function runs with the situation, and each sub-goal that runs plays in turn (attacks, walking or running to the target, turning, strafing, backing off, waiting). Then the character returns to idle. Double-click to show the act's function.
Click: play the act on the character. Double-click: show its function.

The NpcParam row the character runs as. Its ID sets the model; its animation offsets (its own and its resident SpEffects') pick the clips it plays, and its behaviorVariationId picks its BehaviorParam rows.
Picking a battle goal picks the NpcParam row of an NpcThinkParam row that uses the goal, or else the character's first row.

The NpcThinkParam row the goal reads its ai:GetExcelParam(AI_EXCEL_THINK_PARAM_TYPE__field) values from (thinkAttr_doAdmirer, caravanRole, weaponOnAnimId, …).
You can pick any row: its battleGoalID is ignored, because the selected script is the battle goal being simulated. Rows that run this goal are marked.
The NPC's own row: the NpcThinkParam row of its NpcParam ID, or else the first row that runs this battle goal

The result of ai:GetTeamOrder(ORDER_TYPE_Role): the character's role in its team, assigned by the game's team AI.
Most battle goals (570 of ER's role checks) only use their attack weights for the attacker. With thinkAttr_doAdmirer set, a surrounder (ROLE_TYPE_Torimaki) strafes around the target and a spectator (ROLE_TYPE_Kankyaku) hangs back.
The character is its team's attacker (ROLE_TYPE_Attack), like a lone enemy, so it uses its attack acts
The character takes turns as one of a group fighting the same target: the attacker for a while, then a surrounder (ROLE_TYPE_Torimaki) strafing around the target, and so on
The role comes from the Situation's GetTeamOrder input, which you set
How long each turn as the attacker lasts
How long each turn as a surrounder lasts (0: always the attacker)

List only the rows of {0} (the character named in the battle script's file name) and its model variants ({1} to {2}), to switch between them without listing every other enemy.
This setting applies to both the NPC and Think lists. A row belongs to a character by its ID (43000000 is c4300's, 43010000 is c4301's).
Filter by ID, name, chr ID or alias

Each clip plays at its ID plus the first of these offsets the character has a clip for, or else at its own ID.
The resident SpEffects' offsets are tried before the row's animIdOffset2 and animIdOffset.

NpcParam normalChangeModelId shows another model, normalChangeAnimChrId plays another character's animations (and TAE), and normalChangeTexChrId uses another character's textures.
Swapped textures only show where their names match the model's materials, and only if they weren't already loaded.

NpcParam modelDispMask0..31: the mask groups shown (1). The rest are hidden, and a mesh without a group is always shown.
The playing clip's DrawMask events change them from their start, and HideMask and ShowMask events change them while they last.
Turn speed: none (faces the target at once)

NpcParam turnVellocity: how fast the character turns toward the target while it walks, runs, strafes, backs off, or turns on the spot without a turn clip.
During an attack clip, it turns only while the clip's SetTurnSpeed events are active, at their speed (a negative speed uses this value). A clip without them faces the target when it starts.
NpcParam hitRadius: the result of ai:GetMapHitRadius(TARGET_SELF). Scripts subtract it from their act distances (5 - radius) in Goal.Activate and in the act functions.
ai:HasSpecialEffectId(TARGET_SELF, id) is true for these (NpcParam spEffectID0..31). You set other SpEffects yourself; events and the TAE apply them.
Answered by the character: its NpcParam or NpcThinkParam rows, or a SpEffect its TAE applied (see Time Act)
while the event lasts, then {0} s
until the simulation is reset (effectEndurance below 0)

Applied by the TAE's AddSpEffect events: on while the event lasts, then for the SpEffect's effectEndurance.
The battle goal's HasSpecialEffectId(TARGET_SELF, id) is true for them, so the next act is picked with them active.

Goal.Interrupt: what the goal does when something happens mid-act.
It runs automatically when the character's TAE applies a SpEffect the goal observes on itself (INTERUPT_ActivateSpecialEffect). Fire the others by hand.
If it returns true, the act stops, what it queued plays instead, and the simulation picks again once that has played.
Run the Interrupt as if INTERUPT_{0} happened (tested at line {1})
Run the Interrupt as if SpEffect {0} had just been applied (INTERUPT_ActivateSpecialEffect)
The act was interrupted (Goal.Interrupt took it)

The TAE events of the clip the character is playing, stepped along with it.
Effect events spawn their FFX on their dummy poly; bullet events fire their Bullet row (through the character's BehaviorParam) at the target.
The TAE comes from the Time Act Editor (including unsaved edits), and the effects from the FX Editor's bank.
Show the effects spawned by the TAE events and the bullets (needs the FX Editor enabled for the project)

Every effect the character can trigger is prepared before an act plays: the effects of its TAE effect events in all its animations, and its bullets' flight and hit effects (including child bullets). This stops effects stalling when they first show.

Write the {0} Lua binders with unsaved changes into the project. Edited scripts are saved as text (the game loads text Lua), the binder's .luagnl is rebuilt, and every other entry keeps its bytes. Scripts with syntax errors aren't saved.

Become the target and fight the character yourself in first person. The battle goal reads your distance and facing just as it does for a target moved with the gizmo, and your actions reach it as set below.

Walk on the flat ground the characters stand on, using the viewport movement keys and the Map Editor's first person keys. The target is placed at your feet, facing where you look, and hidden while you walk as it.
Walking as the target. Press {0} to pause and release the mouse.
Paused. Click in the viewport to resume, or press {0} again to leave.
Place yourself at the target's feet, looking at the character, with the mouse captured. Press {0} to pause, and again to leave.
Move with the viewport movement keys. {0} to run, {1} to jump, {2} to roll, {3} for estus; left-click attacks and right-click (held) guards; {4} to pause.
Pick the character (NPC) first. There is no one to fight.

How each of your actions reaches the AI: the interrupt it fires as it starts (Goal.Interrupt), and the SpEffects it applies to you for a while (HasSpecialEffectId(TARGET_ENE_0, id) sees them, and a goal that observes one on TARGET_ENE_0 gets INTERUPT_ActivateSpecialEffect).
The SpEffect IDs for rolling, drinking and so on come from the project's data, so set them here. Interrupt types the goal's Interrupt tests for are marked.
Left-click. Fires its interrupt (FindAttack: the AI sees you attack), and also Damaged when the character is within reach in front of you.
Right-click, held. IsTargetGuard(TARGET_ENE_0) is true while held. Its interrupt fires when the guard goes up, and its SpEffects stay on while held.
Drink an estus flask. Fires its interrupt (UseItem).
Roll in the direction you move (or face), covering the distance below over the time below.
Jump and land back on the ground.
How long the action's SpEffects stay on you
How long the guard's SpEffects stay on you after you release it
An attack also fires Damaged (the AI is hit) when the character is within this distance and within 60 degrees of your front
How far an attack reaches, on the ground, from your feet to the character
SpEffect IDs, separated by commas, applied to you when the action starts. Applied when you leave the field (Escape undoes).
{0} pause   LMB attack   RMB guard   {1} estus   {2} roll   {3} jump   {4} run

What the viewport shows of the battle simulation. None of these settings change the simulation: bullets still fly and hit, and distances and aiming are still measured from the target.
